summary: Frontend-only bug-fix verification for navbar/hero-overline overlap on Richa Chandra portfolio. Tested 5 viewports (1920x1080, 1280x650, 1440x720, 768x700, 390x844). At every viewport, navbar bottom sits strictly ABOVE hero overline 'PRODUCT MANAGER — MUMBAI' with positive gap, and the headline 'Building products people can't put down.' is fully rendered and never vertically intersected by the fixed navbar. Navbar (logo + nav links + 'Get in touch' CTA) remains fully visible and functional. Bug fix is CONFIRMED WORKING.

issues: Gap between navbar bottom (98px) and overline (112px) is only 14px — technically no overlap, but visually tight. Consider bumping pt on hero (e.g., pt-32) or reducing navbar height on this breakpoint for extra breathing room.
Navbar height jumps to 98px (vs 78px on other breakpoints) — likely due to nav links wrapping to 2 lines. Worth reviewing responsive layout for md breakpoint.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Increase hero top padding at the md breakpoint (or reduce navbar wrapping on ~768px) — current gap is only 14px on 768x700; still no overlap, but visually cramped.
No blocking action items. Bug fix verified across all requested viewports.
critical_code_review_comments: Hero.jsx uses min-h-[100svh] with pt-28 pb-24 — good fix for short viewports; content can no longer center under the fixed navbar.
Navbar wraps to 98px tall at 768x700 (likely due to nav link layout). Consider hamburger menu or tighter spacing for tablet breakpoint.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Overline is rendered as split text nodes (styled uppercase via CSS letter-spacing/font). Search by lowercase 'product manager' + walk up to a wrapper containing both 'product manager' and 'mumbai' to get accurate bounding box. All bug-fix criteria satisfied.
rca of the issue: Original overlap likely caused by hero using fixed h-[100svh] with vertically centered content — on short viewports (e.g. 1280x650, 1440x720) the centered overline slid up under the fixed 78px navbar. Fix: switched to min-h-[100svh] + pt-28 pb-24 so the top padding pushes content below navbar height. Verified: navbar_bottom < overline_top on all tested viewports (min gap 14px at 768x700, max 185.9px at 1920x1080).
